title: Exact coefficient-preserving ringed module inverse image and standard resolutions
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small in a common universe $u$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R,S$ be ring sheaves on them. Use their module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. An exact coefficient-preserving module inverse-image datum consists of a ringed-topos morphism $f$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], a proof that its actual structural ring map is invertible, an additive functor $F:\operatorname{Mod}(S)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ preserving finite limits and finite colimits [def-galois-exact-functor] [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], and an adjunction $F\dashv f_*$ to the supplied module direct image. For each $R$, use the standard K-injective resolution instance on $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, obtained from its Grothendieck abelian structure [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. On strict towers $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-inverse-system], use the standard Grothendieck K-injective instance transported from the small diagram-site realization. These specify the existing datum and resolution instances; they assert no derived adjunction-square identity.
